blocks.content: Andhra Pradesh has one of the fast-growing economies among Indian states. The state's economy is primarily agrarian but has been diversifying significantly into industry, services, and information technology.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Andhra Pradesh economy is structured around key primary and secondary sectors including Agriculture and Major Crops.
Industrial growth is driven by Major Industries distributed across strategic economic zones.
Key infrastructural pillars include Major Ports facilitating maritime trade and the Power Sector supporting industrial demands.
Special Economic Zones (SEZs) and Industrial Corridors form the backbone of state economic planning and investment.

blocks.content: Agriculture is the backbone of Andhra Pradesh's economy, employing a large proportion of the workforce. The state is called the 'Rice Bowl of India' owing to the fertile Krishna-Godavari delta producing enormous quantities of rice. Andhra Pradesh is one of the top producers of rice, tobacco, cotton, sugarcane, groundnut, chilli peppers, and aquaculture in India.

blocks.content: Andhra Pradesh has a diverse industrial base including pharmaceuticals, cement, power generation, textiles, food processing, petroleum, and information technology.

blocks.content: 5.5 Special Economic Zones (SEZs) and Industrial Corridors

The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) is a major industrial development initiative connecting the two cities. Andhra Pradesh also has several SEZs in Visakhapatnam and Krishnapatnam focusing on IT, pharmaceuticals, and manufacturing. The PCPIR (Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Region) at Visakhapatnam/Kakinada is another major initiative.
